newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesia's Suharto hails Clinton's election win.
newsitem.headline: Indonesia's Suharto hails Clinton's election win.

text.p: Indonesia's President Suharto on Wednesday congratulated Bill Clinton on his re-election to the U.S. presidency, State Secretary Murdiono said.
"President Suharto has sent his congratulations to President Clinton," Murdiono told reporters after a cabinet meeting.

He said Suharto was also convinced that good relations between the two countries would strengthen the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) forum, which is due to meet in the Philippines later this month.
Clinton and Suharto have met at two previous APEC summits and will meet again at the coming summit at Subic Bay.
Murdiono added that while there might be differences of opinion between the two countries, this was normal and could be settled as between friends.
A senior Indonesian Foreign Ministry official earlier said Jakarta expected good bilateral relations between Indonesia and the United States to continue with Clinton's re-election.
"I believe American policy towards Indonesia will not change," Nazaruddin Nasution, director for American affairs at the ministry, told Reuters.
"We know ... the United States would like to strengthen bilateral ties in the fields of investment, trade and ecomic matters," he added.

He said Washington "would like to know more about Indonesia in terms of human rights, democracy". But he described the personal relationship between Clinton and Indonesia's President Suharto as "very good", noting they had met three times over the past three years.
Official sources said they did not expect the foreign funding row involving the Democratic Party during the election campaign to harm relations.
During the election campaign the Republicans raised the question of donations to the Democrats by people connected with Indonesia's Lippo Group, headed by the Riady family.
The official sources noted that Foreign Minister Ali Alatas had said the donations had nothing to do with the Indonesian government, but were the private activity of an Indonesian citizen.
